Her friends also noticed that she developed a red, itchy rash over her face and chest shortly after eating.

Over the past two months, she has been increasingly irritable and has lost interest in soccer, which she previously played with enthusiasm.
She reports feeling tired most of the time despite sleeping more than usual.
Her grades have dropped, and she finds it difficult to concentrate on her homework.
She admits to feeling worthless and has had recurrent thoughts that her family would be better off without her.

lines: Three-month history of persistent sadness, isolation, significant weight loss, and expressions of hopelessness brought to emergency department by parents.

The patient is a 19-year-old female with a history of mild persistent asthma, atopic dermatitis, and allergic rhinitis who was previously evaluated for major depressive disorder with suicidal ideation in July and November 2023, and is brought to the emergency department by her parents due to a 3-month history of persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, and declining academic performance.
Her parents report that she has been isolating herself in her room, has had significant weight loss, and expresses feelings of hopelessness.
She denies any current suicidal ideation but admits to having had thoughts of self-harm two weeks ago, which she did not act upon.
She has no plan for suicide but feels that "everyone would be better off without me." She has no history of psychiatric treatment and expresses doubt that treatment would help her.

encounters.cc: Two-week history of withdrawal, hopelessness, social media posts about wanting to escape life, and giving away possessions.

lines: Two-week history of withdrawal, hopelessness, social media posts about wanting to escape life, and giving away possessions.

The patient is a 19-year-old female with a history of mild persistent asthma, atopic dermatitis, and allergic rhinitis who returns to the emergency department with recurrent psychiatric symptoms following prior evaluations in July 2023, November 2023, and January 2024.
Over the past two weeks, she has become increasingly withdrawn, has expressed feelings of hopelessness, and has lost interest in activities she previously enjoyed.
Her parents also report that she has been posting messages on social media about wanting to "escape life" and has given away several of her prized possessions.
When asked directly about suicidal thoughts, she admits to having a plan to overdose on over-the-counter medications and expresses a desire for help.
Her parents are supportive but express concern about hospitalization and are hesitant to consent to her admission.
